entities.name: Maelgwn ap Rhys
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Maelgwn ap Rhys (c. 1170–1230/31) was a son of Rhys ap Gruffydd (the Lord Rhys) who contested the partition of Deheubarth in south-west Wales, alternately allying with and fighting Anglo-Norman Marcher powers and his own kin. His career unfolds in the violent inheritance politics after the Lord Rhys’s death.

Castles, hostages, and shifting oaths to King John and Welsh rivals defined his rule in parts of Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi. He exemplifies how Welsh royal houses fragmented under English pressure yet remained locally formidable.

Maelgwn is a key actor in early thirteenth-century Deheubarth’s civil strife.
